vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A published CVE does not wait for Monday. Security updates ignore the weekly schedule, the concurrency limits and the cooling period that everything else obeys.

packageRules.description: Mastodon is upgraded by hand, never by a merge. A version bump needs the pre-deployment migration, the image rollout and the post-deployment migration in that order, and Flux applies whatever is on main without knowing any of that. See docs/upgrade-runbook.md.
Images this repository builds. The tag is the commit that produced them, so there is nothing for Renovate to look up.
Everything that runs alongside Mastodon rather than as part of it. Grouped so a quiet week is one pull request instead of six.
Actions and Terraform providers move on their own schedule and are cheap to review together.
A major version is a reading task, not a merge task.

customManagers.description: TOFU_VERSION in the Terraform workflow, which setup-opentofu reads.
GITLEAKS_VERSION in the secret-scan workflow. The pinned sha256 alongside it has to be updated by hand, so these arrive as a prompt to do that rather than as a merge.
